questions.question: The average of 47 consecutive natural numbers is 99. What is the largest number among these numbers?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average of 47 consecutive natural numbers is 99.

Concept used:

A, (A + D), (A + 2D), ....., L is an arithmetic progression with the first term, common difference, and last term A, D, and L respectively.

Sum of the series = (A + L)/2 × N (N = number of terms in the series)

Nth term of the series = A + (N - 1) × D

Calculation:

Let the first number be N.

Since the numbers are consecutive, the common difference is 1 with N being the first term in the arithmetic progression.

So, 47th term = N + (47 - 1) × 1 = N + 46

According to the concept,

{N + (N + 46)}/2 × 47 = 99 × 47

⇒ {N + (N + 46)}/2 = 99

⇒ 2N + 46 = 198

⇒ N = (198 - 46)/2

⇒ N = 76

So, 47th term = 76 + 46 = 122

∴ The largest number is 122.

questions.question: A sum of ₹15,250 is divided among Shrinza, Sheetal and Chirag such that Shrinza receives 40% more than Sheetal and Sheetal receives 40% less than Chirag. What is Chirag's share?
questions.solution:
Given:

A sum of ₹15,250 is divided among Shrinza, Sheetal, and Chirag such that Shrinza receives 40% more than Sheetal and Sheetal receives 40% less than Chirag.

Calculation:

Let's suppose, Chirag receives Rs. x.

⇒ 2.44x = 15250

⇒ x = 15250/2.44

⇒ x = 6250

∴ Chirag's share is Rs. 6250.

questions.question: The ratio between the volumes of Sphere 1 and Sphere 2 is 27 ∶ 64. Find the ratio of the surface areas of Sphere 1 and Sphere 2.
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio between the volumes of Sphere 1 and Sphere 2 is 27 ∶ 64.

Concept used:

1. Volume of a sphere = {4pi R³ over 3} (R is the radius of the sphere)

2. The curved surface of a sphere = 4πR2 (R is the radius of the sphere)

Calculation:

Let the radii of sphere 1 and sphere 2 be r and R respectively.

According to the concept,

4πr³/3 : 4πR3/3 = 27 : 64

⇒ r : R = sqrt[3]{27} : sqrt[3]{64}

⇒ r : R = 3 : 4

So, the radii of sphere 1 and sphere 2 are 3k and 4k respectively. (k = constant)

Now, the ratio of the surface areas of sphere 1 and sphere 2

⇒ 4π × (3k)² : 4π × (4k)2

⇒ 9 : 16

**∴ The ratio of the surface areas of sphere 1 and sphere 2 is 9 : 16.**

questions.question: X and Y are two alloys of copper and aluminium prepared by mixing the metals in the ratio 6 ∶ 5 and 5 ∶ 9, respectively. If equal quantities of the alloys are melted to form a third alloy Z, what ratio of copper and aluminium will be in Z?
questions.solution:
Given:

X and Y are two alloys of copper and aluminium prepared by mixing the metals in the ratio 6 ∶ 5 and 5 ∶ 9, respectively. 

Equal quantities of the alloys are melted to form a third alloy Z.

Calculation:

Let's suppose, k units of each alloy were taken together.

The total quantity of cooper in alloy Z

⇒ Total quantity of cooper in k units of alloy X + Total quantity of cooper in k units of alloy Y

⇒ (6/(6 + 5) × k + 5/(5 + 9) × k)

The total quantity of aluminium in alloy Z

⇒ Total quantity of aluminium in k units of alloy X + Total quantity of aluminium in k units of alloy Y

⇒ (5/(6 + 5) × k + 9/(5 + 9) × k)

Now, the ratio of copper and aluminium will be in Z

⇒ (6/(6 + 5) × k + 5/(5 + 9) × k) : (5/(6 + 5) × k + 9/(5 + 9) × k)

⇒ (6/11 + 5/14) : (5/11 + 9/14)

⇒ 139/154 : 169/154

⇒ 139 ∶ 169

**∴ The ratio of copper and aluminium will be 139 ∶ 169 in Z.**

Distance = Speed × Time

questions.question: What is the chemical name of battery acid?

The correct answer is __**Sulfuric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• The working of the lead-acid battery involves the formation of lead sulphate by oxidation of lead at the anode and reduction of lead dioxide at the cathode.
 
• During battery charge, the lead sulphate is converted back to lead and lead dioxide, releasing sulphuric acid into the electrolyte.
 
• As sulphuric acid is consumed during the discharge process and released during the charging process. 
 
• The specific gravity of the electrolyte changes during battery use and charge.

• **Hinduism **served as inspiration for the** rituals and ideologies **seen in Kalaripayattu.

• **Thai boxing** is another name for muay thai.
 
• It is a combat sport that combines various **clinching maneuvers **with stand-up hitting.
 
• The **"art of eight limbs"** is the name given to this profession.
 
 
 
• **Karate:**

• Under the influence o**f Chinese martial arts,** it evolved from the local Ryukyuan martial arts.

questions.question: Raziya Sultan was the daughter of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iltutmish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raziya Sultan was the first female Muslim ruler of South Asia and ruled from 1236 to 1240.
 
• Raziya was the only daughter among the four children** of Iltutmish**, the third ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Her mother was Turkan Khatoon, the daughter of Qutbuddin Aibak (r.1206-10) – the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish nominated Razia as his successor after the death of his most capable son, Prince Nasiruddin Mahmud.
 
• Various sources confirm that Iltutmish selected Raziya as she was the eldest of his surviving children and had already displayed her deserving political insights.
 
• She was from Turkish Seljuk’s ancestry and came to be the fifth Mumluk Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Raziya’s accession to the throne was solely based on her merit and was a significant departure in the then political climate where the throne was considered a male monopoly.
 
• The Muslim theologians approved her ascension and most of the Turkish nobility, army, and people of Delhi accepted her on the throne is a testimony of the politico-cultural spirit of that age.
 
• Raziya remains one of the most significant icons of women's power in the history of India.
 
• Her chief merit lies in her fearless assertive decisions, her ability to rule by integrating all walks of people, and to rise above the prejudices of her age and times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**The Delhi Sultanate **

 
• It refers to the five Muslim kingdoms of Turkic and Pashtun (Afghan) origin that ruled the territory of Delhi between 1206 and 1526 CE. In the 16th century, the last of their line was overthrown by the Mughals, who established the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• The five dynasties included:
 
 
• the Mamluk Dynasty (1206–1290)
 
• the Khilji Dynasty (1290–1320)
 
• the Tughlaq Dynasty (1320–1414)
 
• the Sayyid Dynasty (1414–1451)
 
• the Afghan Lodi Dynasty (1451–1526)

questions.question: ______ is a technique in which cancer cells are damaged with radiation while limiting the harm to nearby healthy tissue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiotherapy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Radiotherapy to treat cancer:

 
 
• High doses of radiation are used in radiation therapy, also known as radiotherapy, as a cancer treatment to eradicate cancer cells and reduce tumour size.
 
• As with x-rays of your teeth or shattered bones, radiation is utilised at low doses in x-rays to see inside your body.
 
• Radiation therapy damages cancer cells' DNA, which either kills them or limits their growth at high dosages.
 
• Cancer cells that have DNA damage that cannot be repaired either cease proliferating or die.
 
• When the injured cells expire, the body degrades and eliminates them.
 
• But too much radiation can damage tissues by changing cell structure and damaging DNA. This can cause serious health problems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Surgery:

 
 
• Surgery is a medical speciality that employs operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to examine or treat a pathological condition.
 
• Such as a disease or injury, to enhance bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwelcome ruptured areas.
 
 
 
• Chemotherapy ​
 
 
• **Chemotherapy **is a drug treatment that uses powerful chemicals to kill rapidly growing cells in your body.
 
• Chemotherapy is often used to treat cancer because cancer cells grow and multiply much faster than most other cells in the body.
